about: Correction rounds C16-C23 in postmortem form (root cause, detection, fix, regression tests, evidence). Evidence before C22 is the effect published when each fix landed; C22 evidence is computed at build time from data_store/backtest/c22_bridge.csv (replayed on the C23-restated VIX record), the β grid and the stored run; C23 evidence is quoted from the committed C23 artifacts named in each finding. A round may span days (date to date_end). docs/corrections.md is rendered from this file (scripts/render_corrections.py). test_dashboard.py checks that every listed test exists in the suite and every commit is a full SHA dated inside its round.

headline_series.about: Portfolio cumulative return as published after each round; C16 published no portfolio figure; C23 from the stored canonical run.

rounds.title: Methodology audit: look-ahead, a circular feature, retrospective sizing
rounds.detection: Self-audit of the methodology before the result was published.
rounds.effect: The published +19% headline was a label-noise artifact.

findings.flaw: PDV look-ahead bias
findings.root_cause: The PDV model was fitted on the full sample, so every backtest year traded a forecast that had seen its own future.
findings.fix: PDVLinear refitted per backtest year on strictly earlier returns (walk-forward) before it feeds the pdv_iv_spread feature.
findings.evidence: S1/S1C now trade a causal PDV forecast

findings.flaw: Circular classifier feature
findings.root_cause: vvix was a training feature while the R2 label is defined as VVIX above a threshold, so 86.2% accuracy partly measured rule recovery.
findings.fix: vvix removed from the classifier's features; honest accuracy 63.4%.
findings.evidence: Historical C16 figure: honest accuracy 63.4%; C17 then found it lost to the persistence baseline

findings.flaw: Retrospective Kelly netting
findings.root_cause: Correlation and Sharpe multipliers used same-day P&L to size the same day's positions.
findings.fix: Multipliers shifted one session and applied to position size in a second simulation pass, so contracts and costs reflect the real size.
findings.evidence: Ex-ante sizing; no same-day information

findings.flaw: S1C data snooping
findings.root_cause: S1C's direction was chosen after watching S1 fail on 2018–2025; that cannot be undone in code.
findings.fix: Tested on 2013–2017, a window not used to design it (C17 re-ran it under corrected labels): S1C −$333K; the apparent edge was an artifact.
findings.evidence: Pseudo-out-of-sample under C17: S1C −$333K — the apparent edge was an artifact

findings.flaw: S3 arbitrary P&L scale
findings.root_cause: S3's P&L was an assumed 2% per z-unit (no single-stock options data).
findings.fix: Sensitivity run at 0.5% / 1% / 2% / 4% per z-unit; C22 replaced the proxy with the index leg (a short SPX straddle).
findings.evidence: C16 sensitivity run: P&L +$5K…+$52K, win 15–17 of 17 at every scale (before C18, C21 and C22 re-priced every trade and C22 replaced the proxy with the index leg)

rounds.title: Red-team: the classifier against a persistence baseline; margin; an unbounded tail
rounds.detection: Red-team review in the same week as C16.
rounds.effect: The classifier loses to 'predict yesterday's regime' and was demoted from the trading loop; portfolio −9.1% as published after this round.

findings.flaw: Classifier never benchmarked against persistence
findings.root_cause: Regime labels are same-day observables, so yesterday's label is a no-skill baseline; it scored 90.0% on 2020+ against the classifier's 63.4%.
findings.fix: ML demoted to research; the backtest trades the lagged deterministic rule labels.
findings.evidence: 63.4% vs 90.0% — the ML added negative value

findings.flaw: Margin model documented but not enforced
findings.root_cause: MARGIN_RATIO was defined but never applied, so short straddles had unlimited capacity.
findings.fix: Short straddles capped at nav / (0.20 * K * 100) contracts at entry.
findings.evidence: Cost model now matches its documentation

findings.flaw: S1C had no R2 exit
findings.root_cause: An open S1C short straddle could ride a VVIX spike for up to 21 days with no stop.
findings.fix: S1C force-closes when the regime moves into R2, as S1X, S2X and S4 do.
findings.evidence: Worst-case short-gamma exposure now bounded by the R2 rule

findings.flaw: Dead monthly recalibration; a flat 5% hurdle
findings.root_cause: The monthly Heston loop never produced a calibration (no pre-2026 options data) and nothing consumed its output; Sharpe used a flat 5%.
findings.fix: Loop removed; Sharpe and Sortino measured against the per-date ^IRX path (later superseded in C22).
findings.evidence: Backtest claims now match what the code does

rounds.title: Straddles never rolled: one stale-strike position marked past expiry
rounds.detection: Word-by-word audit of the engine's position series: positions never returned to flat.
rounds.effect: Inverted the contrarian thesis: S1 −$1.53M → +$463K, S1C −$97K → −$404K, portfolio −9.1% → −19.0%; S3 unchanged.

findings.flaw: Same-day re-entry kept one straddle alive
findings.root_cause: The state machine re-entered on the day it exited, so the strike was fixed at first entry and the tenor decayed to its 1-day floor: a directional |S - K| bet, not a vol trade. Every P&L figure from C10 to C17 was contaminated.
findings.fix: A forced flat day so positions roll into fresh 30-day ATM straddles.
findings.evidence: Inverted the thesis: S1 −$1.53M → +$463K, S1C −$97K → −$404K, portfolio −9.1% → −19.0%; S3 unchanged

rounds.title: Signal-engine logic fixes and data-gap repair
rounds.detection: Follow-up review of the signal state machines after C18.
rounds.effect: Cleanup; the canonical numbers did not change.

findings.flaw: S2 stop-loss not propagated; dead code; incomplete summaries; data gaps
findings.root_cause: Stop-loss exits did not reach the S2 position; signal summaries skipped sleeves; market data had gaps.
findings.fix: Stops propagate to the S2 position, dead code removed, summaries cover every sleeve, gaps repaired.
findings.evidence: Cleanup — the canonical numbers did not change

rounds.title: The calibration selector rewarded broken data
rounds.detection: The headline fit was traced to a day the VIX feed returned only ^VIX.
rounds.effect: The published 'best calibration' had been the day the VIX feed failed; fits are now gated on at least 3 VIX tenors with provenance recorded.

findings.flaw: Archived fits ranked by SPX RMSE with no data-sufficiency check
findings.root_cause: With one VIX tenor the VIX leg is one point Heston matches exactly, so under-identified joint fits scored best and headlined the site.
findings.fix: Gate on >= 3 VIX tenors; Feller reported as PASS / BINDING / VIOLATED. C22 went further: the headline is the newest gate-passing fit, never the lowest RMSE.
findings.evidence: The published “best calibration” had been the day the VIX feed failed

rounds.title: The cash hurdle was a test fixture; straddles marked a day too rich
rounds.detection: Adversarial audit of the backtest inputs and the daily bot.

findings.flaw: ^IRX history inside the window was seven synthetic test rows
findings.root_cause: test_rates.py wrote np.linspace(0.015, 0.020) into the tracked database and it was forward-filled for five years.
findings.fix: Real ^IRX history loaded (1,809 rows); the suite now works on a private copy and cannot write the tracked database.
findings.evidence: Part of the round's combined effect above; the two backtest fixes were not re-run separately

findings.flaw: First holding day carried no time decay
findings.root_cause: T_rem was computed from the pre-increment day count, so every mark valued the straddle one day too rich, flattering the short side.
findings.fix: Time to expiry decays from the first holding day.
findings.evidence: Part of the round's combined effect above; the two backtest fixes were not re-run separately

findings.flaw: The bot published classifier output as rule labels
findings.root_cause: The daily refresh relabelled regime_labels.parquet with the demoted classifier and refit a frozen option surface.
findings.fix: The bot writes deterministic rule labels and calibrates on a live chain.
findings.evidence: The published labels are the rule's again

rounds.title: Full-system audit: pricing at the VIX, free hedging, two R2 gates, a z-score P&L
rounds.detection: A subsystem-by-subsystem audit (about 270 findings, each reproduced before fixing) after the live calibration failed for a month.

findings.flaw: ATM straddles priced at the VIX
findings.root_cause: The VIX is a 30-day variance-swap rate that contains the skew premium; straddles were priced and marked at it.
findings.fix: ATM vol = β × VIX, with β estimated from stored SPX chains.

findings.flaw: Two R2 gates and a hard-coded VVIX override
findings.root_cause: Published labels used the adaptive gate while the backtest traded a fixed 100-point VVIX gate, and the signal engine OR-ed a VVIX > 100 override onto any labels.
findings.fix: One adaptive gate (rolling 252-day 80th percentile of VVIX) everywhere; no override.

findings.flaw: Free hedging, no carry, sizing off $1M, no-op netting
findings.root_cause: The opening hedge and unwind were free, the book earned no carry, size used $1M instead of the sleeve's NAV, and the netting factor was clipped into a no-op.
findings.fix: Costs charged once each, premium and hedge financed, size off the running sleeve NAV, real netting.

findings.flaw: S3 P&L was a z-score times an assumed 2%
findings.root_cause: The 'survivor' was positive on 99.5% of random-walk null paths: it measured mean reversion of a ratio, not option P&L.
findings.fix: S3 is the index leg of the dispersion trade (a short SPX straddle) on the same engine, with a timing null test.

findings.flaw: PDV spread compared the 30-day VIX with a 1-day forecast
findings.root_cause: The pre-C22 forecast was next-day E|r|, so 'VIX > forecast + 2 vol pts' held on almost every session.
findings.fix: The spread uses a 21-day RMS-vol forecast refitted daily on labels fully observed at the forecast origin.

findings.flaw: Sharpe charged cash twice
findings.root_cause: Option P&L on unfunded collateral is already an excess return; subtracting ^IRX again double-counted it.
findings.fix: Sharpe uses rf = 0 (collateral assumed to earn T-bills), with the T-bill benchmark shown beside it.

findings.flaw: VIX indices fitted as futures; ATM-call anchors; one-expiry live fits
findings.root_cause: The calibrator fitted spot VIX indices with the futures formula, anchored on adjacent ATM calls only, and the daily bot accepted fits from one SPX expiry (9 options) for a month.
findings.fix: Spot-index VIX leg, forward-moneyness z-grid anchors with put-wing quotes, and a gate on expiries, options and the put wing.
findings.evidence: Headline Heston fit replaced; one-expiry fits are rejected by the gate

rounds.effect: Portfolio P&L −$261,206 (C21 as published) → −$216,092 (NAV $783,908), Sharpe −1.80 → −0.88, max drawdown −31.5% → −21.6%, as published in C22; S1 +$693,938 → −$287,644. The waterfall above replays the 15 steps on the C23-restated VIX record, so its last bar is the C23 canonical run.

rounds.title: Vendor data, the calibration's identification, spread-unit evidence and statistical inference
rounds.detection: A reviewer-standard pass over every subsystem in six parallel chains (surface, calibration, statistics, data, UI, engineering), each result measured on the five committed model_version 2 sessions and merged only with the full suite green.
rounds.effect: Portfolio P&L −$216,092 → −$222,177, Sharpe −0.88 → −0.99 (C23 waterfall, data_store/backtest/c23_bridge.csv: 8 VVIX sessions from Cboe −$6,502; 136 Cboe values +$417); 6 of 4,162 rule labels move; the portfolio Sharpe's 95% bootstrap interval is −1.81 to −0.30. The headline Heston fit is unchanged, now reported with its σ profile and rough Heston beside it.

findings.flaw: The labels, backtest and calibrator read Yahoo's copies of the VIX index family
findings.root_cause: Production overlaid Cboe's official closes on vix_daily only; every consumer read vix_term_structure, Yahoo's float32 copies with NULL provenance, NYSE-holiday rows and 8 VVIX sessions missing (forward-filled).
findings.fix: Cboe's index files are the record (Yahoo only as a provisional same-evening row, replaced when Cboe posts); the database cache re-synced from it; the daily job writes Cboe first and reports cross-source differences above 0.25 pts.
findings.evidence: 136 term-structure rows replaced (38 by more than 0.25 pts, 33 of them in the backtest window), 8 VVIX sessions added, 31 holiday rows removed; portfolio −$216,092 → −$222,177 (c23_bridge.csv); labels 2019-08-09, 2020-02-20, 2020-06-11, 2021-05-11 R1 → R2 and 2021-06-09, 2021-07-08 R2 → R1

findings.flaw: The σ ≤ 2 box, not the market, sets the headline fit
findings.root_cause: σ sits on its 2.0 ceiling in 2 of the 5 model_version 2 fits (2026-03-24, 2026-10-16); the page said 4 of 5 parameters are set by the market without saying what the box costs.
findings.fix: A σ profile (the joint loss refitted under caps 1 to 10, κ ≤ 60) and Gauss–Newton identifiability are stored per session and shown; the production box is kept (the NN domain, the vomma shock sizing and the gate depend on it) and its cost is published.
findings.evidence: 2026-10-16: freeing σ gives σ 6.90, κ 27.4, loss −27.7%, out-of-sample RMSE 2.96 → 1.19 vol pts and model VVIX 205 → 113 against the market's 110; on 2026-03-24 the box costs 2.1% of the loss (data_store/calibrations/diagnostics/)

findings.flaw: Model error was never measured against the bid–ask, and quotes were not screened for static arbitrage
findings.root_cause: No per-quote residuals were stored, the calibration chart drew the model only, and nothing screened the stored quotes for static arbitrage.
findings.fix: A surface package: Cohen–Reisinger–Wang screen and l1 repair on HiGHS, an executable-arbitrage certificate, eSSVI and calendar-ordered SVI surfaces, and one scorecard that scores every model on the calibrator's out-of-sample quotes in half-spreads.
findings.evidence: Out-of-sample median |model − mid| over the 5 sessions: Heston 4.4–15.6 half-spreads (3.0–12.3% inside the bid–ask); the arbitrage-free SVI surface 0.45–1.98 (32–80% inside); executable static arbitrage on all 5 sessions, 160–629 quotes per session in an executable row (data_store/surface/)

findings.flaw: The backtest had no statistical inference
findings.root_cause: Sharpe ratios and a 200-path S3 null were published without intervals, deflation for the configurations tried since C10, or exposure-matched nulls for every sleeve.
findings.fix: Stationary-bootstrap intervals, PSR/DSR against a committed trials ledger, Hansen SPA and StepM, CSCV PBO, exposure-matched circular-shift and trade-shuffle nulls for every sleeve, and forecast comparisons (QLIKE, Diebold–Mariano, MCS).
findings.evidence: Portfolio Sharpe −0.99, 95% CI −1.81 to −0.30; S3 timing p 0.078 against 3,550 circular shifts (Holm over 6 sleeves 0.47); Hansen SPA p 0.65 for the published series against cash; S3's largest DSR over every trial count 0.27 (data_store/backtest/inference/summary.json)

findings.flaw: Flat rates in the hedger and the Greeks surface
findings.root_cause: The C7 hedger hard-coded R = 1.5% ('2020 US Treasury'), and the Greeks surface used one median r and q for every maturity, so its 1-year forward was 0.50% below that expiry's parity forward.
findings.fix: A daily Treasury zero curve (bills and par yields, look-ahead gated, refused when more than 7 days old) feeds the calibrator's reference, the chain cleaner, the C7 study and per-maturity Greeks carry.
findings.evidence: C7 cumulative P&L 167.95 → 168.34 index points; Greeks surface 1-year forward 7,931.8 → 7,971.7 (the parity forward); the committed fits recorded ^IRX and are unchanged

findings.flaw: A presentation test could lose a captured session
findings.root_cause: The daily job committed the chain and the fit only if the dashboard tests passed; a test that pinned a value of the committed data failed on the first new fit, and the 2026-10-19 overnight book (accepted three times) was lost.
findings.fix: Separate gates: data tests gate the capture commit, artifact tests the derived artifacts, presentation tests only the deploy; CI simulates the bot's next session before merge.
findings.evidence: No published number moved; the simulated next session (scripts/ci/simulate_next_session.py) found 5 more tests that would have blocked the deploy on the first accepted fit
